basis: Skeletal dysplasia, hypoparathyroidism and microphthalmia define disease; anemia 30-79%. Dental caries 30-79% omitted at cap; brain calcification alone lacks functional damage.

decisions.ocular: primary: microphthalmia is explicitly defining and reported in 5/5 patients; other structural ocular abnormalities support this axis.

basis: Thyroid hormone metabolism defect; delayed bone age and short stature in 2/4 do not establish skeletal damage. Intellectual disability and structural myopathy are occasional, 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: delayed maturation and short stature in 2/4 reflect endocrine growth effects; demonstrated structural myopathy occurs only in 5-29%.

basis: Cerebral motor disorder affecting all four limbs; persistent muscle-tendon shortening and fixed contractures develop in more than 30% over the typical course.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed contractures and structural muscle-tendon shortening affect >30% over the course of quadriplegic cerebral palsy, beyond altered tone alone.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect with encephalopathy/dystonia; neurologic disease, optic pallor and structural kyphoscoliosis reported in 1/1. Very small denominators limit certainty.

decisions.neurologic: involved: encephalopathy, dystonia and tetraparesis are manifestations of the metabolic defect; axial dystonia is documented in 1/1.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural kyphoscoliosis is documented in 1/1, supporting lasting skeletal involvement, although prevalence rests on a single patient.

basis: Seoul hantavirus infection causes the defining renal and hemorrhagic syndrome, including characteristic thrombocytopenia and hemostatic abnormalities.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the hemorrhagic syndrome with characteristic thrombocytopenia and disordered hemostasis is part of the disease definition.

basis: Progressive encephalopathy 80-99%; optic nerve hypoplasia and patent ductus arteriosus each 1/3. Small samples limit certainty. Reflux is separately diagnosed.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: patent ductus arteriosus is an annotated structural cardiovascular defect in 1/3 patients, approximately 33%; the small denominator limits certainty.
decisions.ocular: involved: optic nerve hypoplasia represents structural ocular injury in 1/3 patients, approximately 33%; the small denominator limits certainty.

basis: Central and peripheral neuropathy define disease. Reflux occurs in 5/5 but is separately diagnosed; central apnea is neurologic, and recurrent infections are secondary.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: reflux in 5/5 is a separately diagnosed condition; the supplied evidence does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal tissue damage.

basis: Bilateral renal agenesis, pulmonary hypoplasia and characteristic lower-limb deformities are defining components of the oligohydramnios sequence.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital lower-extremity deformities are explicitly included in the definition of the sequence.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic defect; profound developmental delay and seizures in 2/2, with brain degeneration. Hepatic metal and glycogen deposits lack demonstrated functional damage.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment and seizures occur in 2/2 with documented brain degeneration; they are manifestations of the molecularly defined metabolic defect.

basis: Histiocytic neoplasm with defining bone lesions; endocrine dysfunction 80-99%, cardiovascular infiltration 30-79%. Renal hydronephrosis 30-79% and orbital involvement omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: cardiovascular infiltration occurs in approximately 50-70%, with aortic abnormalities annotated at 30-79%; frequency and severity favor retention.
decisions.renal: none: hydronephrosis at 30-79% supports involvement, but renal disease is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of more frequent, severe cardiovascular involvement.
